## **What should fintech companies look for in RFP software for banking deals?**


Fintech teams should look for six things: answers grounded in approved sources, support for security questionnaires in any format, granular permissions, an approval audit trail, collaboration across time zones and knowledge that stays current.


- **Cited answers from approved sources:** every answer should point back to the SOC 2 report, policy or past response it came from, so reviewers can verify it in seconds.
- **Any questionnaire format:** banks send SIG spreadsheets, Word forms, PDFs and portal questionnaires. The tool should read all of them and write answers back into the original file.
- **Granular permissions and role-based access:** your PCI attestation and penetration test summaries shouldn't be visible to every seller. Look for permissions by content area and by project.
- **Approval audit trail:** who approved which answer, and when, matters when a bank asks you to confirm an answer during reassessment.
- **Collaboration across time zones:** assignments, approvals and automatic reminders replace the email chain with your CISO.
- **Current knowledge:** the tool should flag conflicting or outdated answers before they reach a buyer.

## **Best for teams running a few questionnaires at a time: Arphie**


Arphie is an AI-native RFP and security questionnaire tool that fits fintech teams with a steady, moderate volume of reviews. It drafts answers from documents and websites it keeps in sync, and shows the source behind each answer.


**Best features**


- **Live document and website connectors:** synced sources mean fewer manual uploads when policies change.
- **Source transparency:** answers come with a traceable source and a confidence indicator, so reviewers know what to check.
- **Excel and Word imports:** AI detects questions and sections in uploaded questionnaires.


**Limitations**


- **Pricing isn't published:**[Arphie's pricing](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/arphie-pricing-features-reviews) is quote-based and tied to how many projects you run at once, which is harder to forecast when RFP volume spikes.

- **Smaller review base:** 26 G2 reviews, so there's less peer evidence than for older tools.


**Pricing:** quote-based, priced by concurrent projects.

**Best features**


- **Governed content library:** approval workflows and content ownership suit regulated teams.
- **Word-based document assembly:** builds formatted proposals from templates and approved content.
- **Unlimited users:** Upland prices Qvidian without a per-seat limit.

**Limitations**

## Frequently asked questions about RFP software for fintech


### What’s the best RFP response software for banks and financial services companies with strict compliance requirements?


Inventive AI is the best fit, because it only drafts from approved company content and shows the source behind every answer. Compliance teams can verify a claim in seconds, and nothing from the open web or model memory reaches a regulated buyer. Large banks and insurers with long-established proposal teams also use Qvidian and Responsive.


### Which RFP solutions include granular permission controls and role-based access?


Inventive AI, Loopio, Responsive and Qvidian all offer role-based access, and Conveyor adds access controls on each document in its trust center. When you compare them, check whether permissions work at the content level and the project level, since that's what keeps penetration test results and pricing away from the wrong people.


### Which RFP platforms work best for global teams across time zones?


Pick a platform priced without per-seat limits, so every SME in every region can contribute. Inventive AI includes unlimited users on its $830/month plan and AutoRFP.ai includes them on every plan. Then check for question-level assignments and automatic reminders, which keep work moving while half the team is offline.


### How do I choose the best RFP software for my team?


Start with your mix: count how many RFPs and how many security questionnaires you answered last quarter. Then match the pricing model to that volume. AutoRFP.ai caps projects per year, Arphie prices by concurrent projects, and Inventive AI includes unlimited users, so the same tool can be cheap for one team and expensive for another.


### What's the difference between an RFP, an RFI and a security questionnaire?


An RFI gathers general information to build a shortlist, an RFP asks for a full proposal with pricing and scope, and a security questionnaire tests how you protect the buyer's data. Fintechs often get all three from the same bank in one deal cycle.


### What is a DDQ, and how is it different from a security questionnaire?


A due diligence questionnaire (DDQ) covers your whole business: ownership, financial health, legal and regulatory standing, compliance programs and operations. A security questionnaire focuses only on information security controls, so a DDQ usually contains a security section rather than the other way around.


### What's the difference between SOC 2 Type I and Type II for fintech vendors?


A SOC 2 Type I report checks whether your controls are designed correctly at a single point in time. A Type II report tests whether those controls actually operated over a period, usually 3 to 12 months, which is why banks give it more weight.


### What is a bridge letter in a SOC 2 review?


A bridge letter, sometimes called a gap letter, is a statement from your management covering the time between the end of your last SOC 2 audit period and today. It confirms no material control changes happened, and banks ask for it when your report is a few months old.


### Which PCI SAQ does a fintech fill out?


It depends on how you handle card data. Merchants that fully outsource payments often qualify for SAQ A, while service providers that are eligible to self-assess use SAQ D for service providers. Larger service providers need a Report on Compliance from a QSA.


### Can a trust center replace security questionnaires?


A trust center cuts down on questionnaires but rarely replaces them. Conveyor's own research found that 46% of buyers still sent a questionnaire after downloading documents from a vendor's trust portal, so you'll want questionnaire automation alongside it.


### What is an RFP in banking?


An RFP in banking is the formal request a bank sends when it wants to buy a product or service, such as a digital banking platform, payments processing or a compliance tool. Vendors reply with a proposal covering scope, pricing and implementation. Fintechs usually get a security questionnaire and a vendor due diligence form alongside it.
